_readme: Project changelog + version ledger. `app_version` bumps on every Claude-assisted change; `strategy_versions` bump ONLY when an engine's tradeable parameters, gates or detectors change. lib/version.py is the read API; the engines stamp these onto every position, so a trade can always be traced back to the code that opened it. Entries are newest-first. Entries with source='reconstructed' were rebuilt from session notes on 2026-08-21 (before the ledger existed) and their exact dates are best-effort; source='live' entries were written at the time of the change.

signals.note: Original strict-pullback entry: down 2 days + bottom 20% of 5d range + RSI<35 + ret_20d>-15%. Retired as -EV (needs 80% WR, delivers ~60%).
Switched to the backtest-validated mean-reversion setup: DoD <= -1%, no-Friday, not-at-5d-high. Break-even WR 33.3%.
SL widened -1.0% -> -2.0% to survive opening volatility. Never re-backtested; moved break-even WR 33.3% -> 50.0%.

SL cooldown cut 7d -> 1d (same-day block only). CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this row previously also claimed a pattern-confluence entry gate. live_signals.py has never contained one — `git log --all -S confluence -- live_signals.py` is empty across every commit. CONFLUENCE_REQUIRED exists only in live_patterns.py (added in 51acb24); requiring a Patterns fire alongside a Signals candidate is live_cross's entire job, not something Signals ever did. The claim came from the 2026-08-21 ledger reconstruction conflating the engines.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard
signals.note: Close-settle gate fixed (5-min tolerance) restoring the EOD sweep, and positions >4d past target now book STALE at market instead of a synthetic TP/SL fill. CORRECTED 2026-08-24: 'confluence required' removed from params — see sig-4.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, AUTO-ENTRY at ask, no entry after 16:30
signals.note: Primary signals auto-enter at ask again, reverting the 2026-05-27 manual-only flow under which the wallet held zero open positions. Added a 16:30 late-entry cutoff to match patterns/cross — the manual flow never needed one because good-for-the-day limit orders expired at the close. Entry filter itself (DoD <= -1%, not-at-5d-high, no-Friday, ret_20d > -15%) and TP/SL/hold are unchanged; what changed is that clearing the filter now buys instead of surfacing.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, AUTO-ENTRY at ask, no entry after 16:30
signals.note: Stop restored -2.0% -> -1.0%, back to the backtested pair (40.9% WR, +72 SEK/trade, profitable 10 of 11 years). The -2.0% stop ran from 2026-05-25, was widened to survive opening volatility, was never re-backtested, and moved break-even WR from 33.3% to 50.0%; the engine delivered 43.8% (7W/9L over 16 scored) and -388 SEK/trade against it. Signals only — Patterns (pat-3) and Cross (x-2) still run -2.0%, which keeps Patterns as a control group on the same TP/hold with different entry logic.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, AUTO-ENTRY at ask, no entry after 16:30, liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
signals.note: Two new entry gates. Liquidity: a position may not exceed 5% of the name's median daily volume (from ohlc/), falling back to today's cumulative volume when no history exists; 13 of the 158-name universe now fail it, all A/D-class or genuinely thin listings. Cross-wallet dedupe: a company stem held in the Patterns or Cross wallet is no longer buyable here.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, CLOSE-CONFIRMED ENTRY (one post-close pass, filled at the official close), liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
signals.note: Entries move off the intraday tick and onto the confirmed close. Measured by replaying this exact filter over 64 entry days of minute data (2026-04-30..2026-08-20), varying only the execution regime: close entry + close exit n=2346 46.6% WR +0.372%/trade; close entry + intraday exit n=2346 43.5% WR +0.301%; intraday entry + intraday exit (sig-8) n=4352 40.2% WR +0.202%. Entering intraday nearly doubles the trade count by taking names that dip 1% and recover before the close - trades the backtest never saw - and costs ~45% of the per-trade edge. Chosen because the wallet is slot-constrained rather than signal-constrained (6 open against a 35k floor), so per-trade quality outranks signal count. NOT a fix for the sig-8 result: at 7W/16L against a true 40.2%, P(<=7 wins in 23) = 23%, i.e. ordinary variance - roughly 200 trades are needed before the win rate separates from the 33.3% break-even at all. Carries a mild lookahead (the close both triggers the entry and sets the fill), the same assumption the arm-B figure was measured under; the real-world equivalent is a closing-auction order.

signals.params: TP +3.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, DoD <= -2.0%, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, close-confirmed entry, liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
signals.note: Retune of the two parameters that actually carry edge, after the -1% stop was questioned and re-tested. Method: the same entry filter swept over two independent samples — 11 years of daily closes for the 158-name large-cap universe (n=68,905 close-to-close trades, 2016-01-01 onward) and true tick-order fills reconstructed from 3.4M minute prints (n=2,723, 2026-04-30..2026-09-03), the latter walking every print in sequence so TP/SL ordering inside a bar is real rather than assumed. TAKE-PROFIT +2% -> +3%: 11y 45.8% WR +0.353%/trade -> 41.1% +0.545%; tick 44.7% +0.335% -> 37.4% +0.455%. Monotonic out to +4% on both samples, but return per day-of-held-capital flattens after +3%, and this wallet is capital-constrained. DOD_THRESHOLD -1% -> -2%: 11y +0.353% -> +0.385%; tick +0.335% -> +0.390%; also monotonic (-3% gives +0.423% / +0.434%). Took -2% rather than -3% because -3% fires only ~3x/day across the universe against ~6.6x while scoring +0.267%/capital-day vs +0.231% — the wallet is slot-constrained (6 open, 581k idle), so candidate starvation costs more than the extra per-trade edge earns. Combined: +0.143% -> +0.231% per capital-day, every one of the 11 years positive (+0.48%..+0.83%). STOP DELIBERATELY UNCHANGED at -1%: widening to -2% was the actual request, and it is wrong. Live record splits cleanly by the stop in force — the -2% era (sig-3/4/6) ran n=27 33.3% WR -0.85%/trade -16,025 SEK against the -1% era (sig-7/8/9) n=40 35.0% +0.05% +1,638 SEK, and break-even WR moves from 33.3% to 50.0%, which this engine has never sustained. An OHLC replay of the current 40 trades under a -2% stop lifts win rate 37.5% -> 50.0% (5 of 26 stop-outs do recover, so the shake-out intuition is real) but cuts per-trade edge +0.125% -> +0.026%, landing exactly on break-even. On tick data the stop curve is a shallow U (-0.5% +0.378% | -1% +0.335% | -2% +0.299% | -3% +0.342%), i.e. the stop only trades win rate against loss size and is not a lever at all; the monotonic 'tighter is better' seen on close-only data is an artefact of never observing an intraday touch. Two hypotheses were tested and REJECTED rather than shipped: that the most-negative-DoD-first candidate ranking was inverted (it is not — deep down-days are the best bucket on both samples, +0.423%/+0.434% at -3%), and that a DoD *band* beat a threshold (a 40-trade live slice suggested -3%..-1.5% was a sweet spot; on 68,905 trades the band is flat-to-worse, so that slice was noise). Expect ~42% win rate against ~46% before, i.e. visibly more red for more money. Caveat carried forward: live runs +0.05%/trade against a +0.35% backtest, so the ranking of these parameters is what transfers, not the magnitudes.

signals.params: TP +3.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, DoD <= -2%, no-Friday, not-at-5d-high
signals.note: Audit batch 2. Stop-loss fills at min(market, stop) instead of always at the stop — every prior stop-out booked a price that, on a gap-down, never traded. Real trading-holiday calendar behind add_trading_days/trading_days_between (holidays were counted as sessions, shortening a 7-day hold to as few as 4). Cross's wallet no longer vetoes Signals entries. Force-entry overrides no longer published as signal_check passes. No TP/SL level or hold-period change.

signals.params: TP +3.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, DoD <= -2%, no-Friday, not-at-5d-high, close-confirmed entry bounded to close+60min
signals.note: Bounds WHEN the close-confirmed entry pass may fire. Filling at the official close is justified in sig-9 as 'the real-world equivalent of a closing-auction order' — an order that must be submitted by ~17:25. But close_confirmed_entry_ready() had no upper bound: it required only after-the-close, feed-settled, trading-day and not-already-scanned. Observed fire times across the 29 close-confirmed entries were 17:45, 18:01, 18:04, 18:05 and, on 2026-09-03, 19:57 — five entries booked at the 17:30 close price two and a half hours after it, by which point the US session had been open ~3.5h and any post-close Nordic news had landed. That is information no auction order could have had, i.e. lookahead beyond what the sig-9 measurement covered. Past the cutoff the day is now SKIPPED, not entered late. Expressed as ENTRY_WINDOW_MINUTES = 60 minutes AFTER THE CLOSE rather than a wall-clock 18:30: on a 13:00 half-day an absolute 18:30 would have permitted a decision 5.5h after the close, the exact thing the bound exists to prevent. On an ordinary session close+60 == 18:30, identical to EOD_WINDOW_END. An unbounded pass was originally deliberate — a fixed window produced zero entries on 2026-08-31 when the Mac slept 16:12-18:04 — but that reasoning is obsolete: `pmset -g sched` shows `wakepoweron at 5:48PM weekdays only` and the plist carries a 17:50 Mon-Fri StartCalendarInterval alongside StartInterval 180, so the window is reached unattended. The feed runs ~16 min behind (state's own data_lag: 963s against a probe trade at 17:29:48), so the close is not visible until ~17:46 and the usable runway is ~45 min at a 3-minute cadence, i.e. ~14 attempts. NOT a fix for a bug: entering after the close is the sig-9 design and is worth ~45% of per-trade edge over intraday entry (close+close +0.372%/trade vs intraday +0.202%, n=2,346 vs 4,352). The owner's 'nothing after 17:15' cannot be combined with it at all — at 17:15 wall clock the feed only shows ~16:59 prices, so buying pre-close and buying at the confirmed close are mutually exclusive.

patterns.note: Engine launched. Bullish Engulfing, Morning Star, Piercing Line, Three White Soldiers, Tweezer Bottom, Hammer on intraday-aggregated daily bars.

patterns.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, 5 entry-eligible patterns, STALE guard, liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
patterns.note: Same two gates as sig-8. Motivated by this engine's 2026-08-24 Electrolux A fill: 2,380 shares against a 4,460-share day, 53% of all volume, on a quote that never moved off the fill price.

Audit batch 1. Detector exceptions are recorded and surfaced instead of swallowed per-stock. A non-positive live quote is tagged stale, so it can no longer book a phantom stop-loss. An unreadable history CSV now disqualifies the name rather than silently skipping the -15% crash guard. No TP/SL/hold or detector-logic change.
